chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from one of his companions, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Any believer who preserves the obligatory prayers and prays them at their proper time, he is not among the oblivious (unaware) ones.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean for a believer to be 'not among the oblivious' in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni uses this narration from Imam al-Sadiq to establish a direct correlation between ritual discipline and spiritual presence of mind, defining the 'ghafilin' not merely as negligent but as those lacking divine awareness. This hadith is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for emphasizing that the validity of faith is intrinsically tied to the punctual observance of the five daily prayers, serving as a primary indicator of a believer's spiritual state.
